parts.text: Which claim best explains floating or sinking here?

options.text: Density matters more than size or apparent heaviness alone; ice floats because it is less dense than liquid water.
The iron rod feels heavier only because it is larger than the wooden stick.
Ice floats because it is denser than liquid water.
Any object that feels heavy must sink in liquid water, even if its density is low.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Dev holds a wooden stick and an iron rod of the same size; the iron rod feels heavier. Later he sees a piece of ice floating on liquid water.

part_answers.answer: Floating or sinking depends on density compared with the liquid, not on size or how heavy the object feels alone.

teacher.key_rationale: Density, not size or apparent heaviness alone, decides floating or sinking; ice is less dense than liquid water. Claiming size alone, reversing ice density, or saying heaviness forces sinking all miss that hinge.
